narrative.overview:
Troop 813 HQ is a light, plain working tool in troop burgundy. The Kiosk asks one question per screen and makes the person's name the hero, set in burgundy condensed capitals large enough to read at arm's length on a shared tablet. The Leader screens carry the same world at phone density: a text-only shell bar, a tab bar, lists drawn as one bordered card with a row per item, soft status pills, and large condensed counts.

Everything sits on a near-white, faintly rose-tinted ground with white surfaces and hairline borders. There is no decoration beyond the troop's monoline logo badge, shown large on the lock, sign-in and waiting screens only. Icons are functional, not decorative: thin-weight Phosphor line icons, whose fine stroke echoes the logo's monoline drawing, label the Leader tabs and Roster row actions. Colour carries meaning: burgundy marks the brand, the current choice and the main action; green, amber and red appear only as state. Both surfaces ship light and dark themes from the same tokens.

The world was pinned by the user from the prototypes (`prototype/kiosk-flow`, `prototype/leader-screens`), with troop burgundy replacing the prototype's green. It refuses two things: the visitor-kiosk grid of identical cards as the main Kiosk experience, and the admin-dashboard look (sidebars, tables, KPI tiles) on the Leader screens.
keyCharacteristics: Condensed display (Barlow Condensed) over a legibility-first body (Atkinson Hyperlegible).
One burgundy accent; green only for success and Going.
Thin Phosphor line icons on Leader navigation and row actions, always paired with a text name.
Flat: white cards on a tinted ground, 1px or 2px outlines, no drop shadows.
Two densities from one token set: Kiosk at a 1.25rem base with 4rem targets, Leader at 1rem with 2.75rem targets.
Light and dark themes; in dark mode the accent splits into light-rose text and deep-burgundy fills.

rules.name: The Green Means Going Rule
rules.body: Green (`ok`) appears only for success and Going. Burgundy is the accent; never use green as a brand colour, a link or a primary button.

rules.name: The Text-Versus-Fill Rule
rules.body: Use `--accent` for burgundy text and strokes and `--fill` (with `--fill-ink`) for burgundy backgrounds. In dark mode the accent becomes a light rose for legible text on the dark ground while fills stay deep burgundy with white text; using `--accent` as a background breaks dark mode.

rules.name: The oklch Source Rule
rules.body: Colours are authored in oklch. Hex appears only where a platform field requires it (the manifest and `theme-color`).

rules.name: The Condensed For Names And Numbers Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed sets names, headings, counts and the shell label. Everything a person reads as a sentence, including the Kiosk's questions and all buttons, is Atkinson Hyperlegible.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Times, attendance counts and big stats use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Two Densities Rule
rules.body: One token set, two densities: Kiosk targets are at least 4rem tall on a 1.25rem base; Leader targets are at least 2.75rem tall on a 1rem base. A new Kiosk screen uses the Kiosk vocabulary; a new Leader screen uses `leader.css`.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Separate layers with `--surface` against `--bg` and a `--line` border, never with a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Crest Not Icon Rule
rules.body: The logo is used at 10rem or larger, never as a small icon. Its trees, stars and lettering cannot render legibly at around 32px at 1x, so shell bars carry the troop name as text instead.

rules.name: The Thin Icons Need Room Rule
rules.body: Use icons at 1.5rem or larger; the thin weight goes faint below that at 1x. An icon never stands alone without an accessible name, and the logo is never an icon.

rules.name: The Zero-Specificity Rule
rules.body: Shared styles carry no weight so a screen's own styles always win. The base element rules in `app.css` (headings, paragraphs, form controls, buttons, links, `:focus-visible`) sit inside `:where()`. The Kiosk's shared vocabulary in `Kiosk.svelte` puts the `.kiosk` scope inside `:where()`, so those rules weigh only as much as their target selector and any scoped class in a Kiosk screen beats them. Every selector in `leader.css` sits wholly inside `:where(.leader …)`, so it has zero specificity: a component's `<style>` always wins, and within `leader.css` the later rule wins. Pseudo-elements cannot go inside `:where()`, so those few rules keep a normal selector. Breaking this (an unwrapped shared selector) has caused real bugs where shared rules overrode screen styles.

dos: Do author every colour as an oklch custom property in `app.css`, with a dark-mode value, and reference it with `var(--…)`.
Do use `--accent` for burgundy text and `--fill` / `--fill-ink` for burgundy backgrounds.
Do keep green (`--ok`) for success and Going, amber (`--warn`) for warnings, red (`--bad`) for problems and Not going.
Do wrap every new shared rule in `:where()` (the whole selector in `leader.css`, the `.kiosk` scope in the Kiosk vocabulary) so screen styles override it and source order decides.
Do give Kiosk controls at least a 4rem height and Leader controls at least 2.75rem.
Do draw lists on the Leader screens as one bordered card with a row per item.
Do pair state colour with a shape or text (check mark, pill label, dashed outline) so meaning never relies on colour alone.
Do gate motion behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and start entrances from a visible state.
Do use the logo through `Logo.svelte` (it follows the text colour), at 12rem on Kiosk lock screens and 10rem on gate pages.
Do use Phosphor icons at weight `thin`, 1.5rem or larger, `aria-hidden="true"`, with the control named by its text or `aria-label`.
Do use fictional names from `bun run seed` in any mock, fixture or screenshot.
donts: Don't use green as a brand or accent colour, or burgundy for success.
Don't use `--accent` as a background fill; it turns light rose in dark mode.
Don't add drop shadows; the inset tab marker is the only box-shadow.
Don't add a shared selector outside `:where()`.
Don't mix icon sets or weights, or use emoji or text glyphs as icons.
Don't make a grid of identical cards the main Kiosk experience; the Handoff's single big name is the main screen and the name list stays secondary.
Don't build Leader screens as an admin dashboard: no sidebars, data tables or KPI tiles.
Don't use the logo below 10rem or as a small icon in a bar, button or tab.
Don't put real Scout names in designs, fixtures or screenshots.
Don't hard-code hex colours in CSS; hex lives only in the manifest and `theme-color`.
